title: TokenRepel: Generating Diverse Image Sets Without Compromising Quality
claim: A method combines a geometric repulsion step with a density-preserving projection, applied at specific points inside each network layer.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked geometric sketches left, vertical flow chart right
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), top left, shows token repulsion. A grid of yellow circles (Image 1 tokens) and one of red triangles (Image 2 tokens) sits next to a blue density map. Small arrows push the circles away from the triangles. Beside it, a vector diagram on a dashed unit circle shows the repulsion step. The vector h-hat goes to h' along a blue gradient arrow, with angles θ and δ marked in red. Panel (b), bottom left, shows density preservation. An orange contour map shows a green dashed score arrow and a black repelled-score arrow. Next to it, a projection diagram uses a red arrow to bring the update into a shaded half-space. Panel (c), right, is a vertical pipeline. Hidden states (blue) go through Attention to attention output (orange), then Token repulsion (red box), then MLP + Residual to layer output (green), then Token density preservation (blue box).
caption: Illustration of our TokenRepel algorithm. \subref{fig:repel_repulsion} Left: The tokens of Image 1 are repelled by taking a negative gradient step induced by the distribution formed from the tokens of the other images. \subref{fig:repel_repulsion} Right: Update formulation for $h_{ij}$, where $\bar{\mu}(\hat{h}_{ij})$ denotes the weighted mean of the other image tokens with respect to their cosine similarity to $h_{ij}$. \subref{fig:repel_preservation} Left: Contours representing the learned data distribution of the generative model, a green dashed arrow representing the original score, and a black solid arrow representing the score after applying token repulsion. \subref{fig:repel_preservation} Right: The refinement process applied to $\nabla \log p^r_t(x_t)$ to project it into the higher-density half-space (red solid arrow). \subref{fig:repel_pipeline} Locations of these two operations inside a transformer layer.
abstract: We present an inference-time approach that enhances the visual diversity of image sets generated by text-to-image models, without compromising the average image quality. Our method leverages the intrinsic geometry of hidden representations in pretrained models to diversify images generated from the same prompt. First, we introduce a token repulsion mechanism that increases the angle between feature tokens across samples. It takes a negative Riemannian gradient step on a von Mises-Fisher mixture distribution of tokens on the unit hypersphere. Second, to preserve the quality of each output image, we propose a token density preservation mechanism that projects the repulsion-induced prediction change onto a half-space aligned with the model's score direction. This encourages the updates to remain within the high-density regions learned by the generative model. We further extend this mechanism to the output of each intermediate layer, enabling finer-grained iterative guidance. We evaluate our method on three types of pretrained text-to-image models. Experiments show substantial gains in visual diversity under identical prompts, while maintaining a comparable level of image fidelity.
